reviews.text: So thankful for Pawsitive Vet! Really nice staff, Dr. Perry was great, she explained everything and took the time to answer our questions. Affordable and I didn’t feel like they are upselling unnecessarily. Would highly, highly recommend!

I went with my cat when she had a concerning nail injury. The vet took her to the back and when she came back, my cat was so hostile, to a degree she’s never been. That’s fine, though, I guess the exam made her angry, right? Wrong, there in fact was no exam at all. The vet just prescribed some medicine and sent me on my way to bring her in again, which means when I come in next time the visit should be covered, right, since the vet couldn’t do it the first time? Wrong, I was told I would have to pay an examination fee AGAIN when no examination was done the first time. I took her someplace else and her nail has since healed, I just feel it’s my responsibility to share my experience so others can be spared after a $200 visit that did basically nothing for my pet. I would avoid this veterinary practice, definitely did not make my cat feel safe and I think could be more transparent with what we’re paying for/have to pay at the next visit. Also, I was told I would get a call back with more info about how much I can expect to pay after the receptionist confirmed with the vet, never got the call.

My cat was a patient here and was dying. She was suffering and couldn't get out of bed. They were "all booked up" and that was the end of the conversation. I had to go to the ER to have her put to sleep. The web site says to call if it's an emergency. But calling did nothing.

I will get another cat. But I won't be bringing her here.
The staff is so kind and sweet and they're very attentive to my fur baby

Checkups for two cats with vaccines $419. Vet recommended that we buy a cat food through them, $$$.
The people and the vet are nice, professional.

My dog was a patient here for 7 years before we moved away. My dog loved it here so much he would frequently drag me to Pawsitive on walks.

When he had a serious illness, they were so kind and supportive. I had to bring him in every week for a while and they kept the charges to a minimum, this is a very affordable vet where animal welfare is central to the practice.

I’m sad that my dog can no longer be a patient here but I highly recommend them!

Took our cat here for years. The vets and receptionists are the best and this was the only vet in brooklyn we felt like got adequate care for our high-need pet without feeling taken advantage of. They're responsive and committed to actually caring for your pets and providing treatment- you can tell they are all animal-lovers first. Dr Perry and Dr Fuzhailov are extremely knowledgeable. I recommend this clinic wherever I can.

Worst place to take your pet they take extremely extra time for everything  they ask you to come earlier and keep you waiting for so long plus they don't know how to give the shops make pet uncomfortable

Their tech mishandled my dog while taking x-rays and exacerbated my dog’s luxating
patella. The lady took my dog to the back and when she came out she was holding my dog close to her chest with her hand concealing my dog’s hind leg and spoke to me casually about the x-ray results. I asked her to put my dog down and MY DOG WAS LIMPING. (the hind leg’s knee cap would occasionally pop in and out of place, which was typical of the dog breed, but this time my dog WAS LIMPING FOR MONTHS!!)

I CAUTION OTHERS TO DO RESEARCH AND READ THE 1 STAR REVIEWS FIRST FOR ANY VET. THIS PLACE ISN’T THE BEST FOR ANY IMPORTANT DIAGNOSES OR PROCEDURES.

Beware!

Dr. Coletti, Taylor, and the entire team are amazing. Recently switched to PAWSitive from a franchise vet and it’s been the best thing for our two pups. The team is so patient and caring. We were beyond worried when our oldest, a rugged, noisy, mostly invincible terrier mix came down with a nasty stomach thing. Dr. Coletti was able to diagnose him as having some intestinal irritation and just needing some meds and probiotics and sn injection of fluids. By the evening following the appointment he was mostly back to being his troublemaker self. PAWSitive also went out of their way to fit us in first thing in the AM the day after I called. Highly recommend.

Since switching to PAWsitive veterinary I feel far more confident that my cat is going to receive the care she needs when she is sick. 2 years ago my cat was diagnosed with asthma and Dr. F has been such a vital source of comfort and clarity for me. In moments of panic she generously made herself available and has ensured that my sweet cat is safe and healthy. At points when I felt my concerns may have been overreactions Dr. F has listened patiently and validated my feelings. Each and every person in the office cares a great deal about the pets they look after. Special thanks to Anita and Dawn who are warm hearted angels that go above and beyond to keep the office running. So many thanks to them! Best vet in Brooklyn!
DO NOT GO HERE.

I still feel angry about the level of care we received from Pawsitive, which was our vet for several years until we left.

Look, if you’re reading this, I suspect that you’ll agree that pets are family members and we want the absolute best for them. And I guess when you’re reading a review you never know if the person is just totally crazy or whatever. You love your dog and you bring them to the vet if there are issues. Things that they waved us off about ended up being a big deal, medically and financially, and we ended up deciding to find a different vet.

After we'd been there for a while, they pushed for us to get a bunch of blood tests for our dog, then took eight weeks to get back to us— when we finally got a hold of them, there were issues to discuss in the results. Not sure why they didn’t leave a message (we work in schools so… can’t just pick up during the day.) But I think we just felt like… you didn't call us about this? After 8 weeks?

My wife’s had our dog since she was 18, and the doctor treated her like she was being a nag. It always felt like they were irritated with our questions and pushing us out the door.  The last straw was when our dog got sick and they brushed it off—he collapsed later that night and we ended up at VERG Emergency. We were regular clients for at least 2 years– and parted with a non-trivial amount of money for a level of care that was consistently harried and dismissive. And again– like, hearing, "Your dog is fine," hours before you have to take him to the emergency room is just– frustrating.

I’m grateful to have found a new place where they welcome asking questions, where the people are kind and friendly. In addition to the very frustrating medical issues, it was just really not a welcoming or nice space to be in on an olfactory or interpersonal level.

Anyway, I guess I can’t really say I'm not for absolutely letting it rip on a Google Maps review because obviously I’m doing that right now, but I get mad when I think about the low quality of care that we got (significant quantity, I’ll add). People deserve and can find care for their pets at vets that will love your animal, encourage your questions, balance thoroughness with a good and straightforward discussion of costs. I'm sure it's a stressful and difficult job– lord knows I don't have to express anyone's anal glands at my job. But I just think, you can find people who will care for your pet with kindness and love- they're out there. And I say all of this because I hope people are able to find that for their pets.

I am usually not the type to jeopardize anyone’s job or leave a negative review, but I had to for this company. This was my first and LAST visit. I was recommended by a friend, but I will not be coming back—and I will warn other pet parents as well. I’d rather take an hour train ride to a trustworthy vet than walk 15 minutes from my home to this one.

Now let me get into it. For a veterinary office that is supposed to care for animals, it felt clear they were more interested in money than my dog’s well-being.

My dog has been experiencing skin irritation, so I decided to give Pawsitive Veterinary a try. Worst decision ever. The front desk staff was polite, but the vet, Dr. Peterson, was shockingly unprofessional. His attitude and appearance were lazy, careless, and nonchalant. When I asked for suggestions, he actually laughed. Instead of offering real answers, he said, “It could be this, it could be that, maybe this, maybe that.” I specifically mentioned doing a blood test, and he brushed it off with no urgency, saying it wasn’t necessary. He seemed unsure of everything and gave me no confidence whatsoever.

He then suggested an injection and shampoo, saying it “might help for a month” and that I’d likely need to come back for more expensive tests later. Essentially, he was asking me to spend $299 that day, only to spend even more later. He barely examined my dog—just brushed his hand over her scars without checking anything properly. When I asked questions, he had no answers. Finally, he said the treatment would work “immediately, within 48 hours” and left the room…never to return. I was left confused, frustrated, and with no trust in his care.

I told his assistant how unprofessional and unclear he was. Unlike him, she showed genuine concern and empathy. Sadly, it made me realize this was probably normal behavior for him.

I left with the treatment, against my better judgment, because I just wanted relief for my pup. But days later, nothing improved. She was still scratching, her skin unchanged, and the shampoo made no difference. $299 for nothing. On top of that, there was no check-up call, no follow-up, no concern.

I emailed them with photos of my dog’s worsening condition. The secretary told me the doctor wouldn’t be available until Thursday. Thursday came—still no response. When I followed up again, they only offered me another appointment with their “lead doctor” Dr. Perry…for an additional cost. At that point it was obvious: they care more about money than pets.

I canceled and went to another vet in Ridgewood, an hour away from Brooklyn. That vet took immediate action, treated my pup correctly, and she is now feeling 1000x better.

⚠️ Please, do not take your pet to Pawsitive Veterinary. They lack professionalism, empathy, and urgency. Do not let them touch your furry family members. Save your time, your money, and most importantly, your pet’s health—go elsewhere.

Dr Coletti and team were amazingly kind over a two day heart break as we learned that our kitty had no chance with cancer. They were incredibly humane, thoughtful and caring from x-rays and blood work to sharing our last moments with our sweet little lady kitty. Thank you Dr Coletti and the rest of the Pawsitive team.

My cat is 20 years old so I am usually nervous about exposing her to new people or putting her through a lot of stress. Dr. Colletti and the vet techs here are always extremely gentle with her even when she gets cranky. Dr. Coletti is very knowledgeable and she really has your pet's best interest in mind. All the staff there are wonderful and it's very clean. Not that it matters business wise but the office has a very early 90s type of feel that I like and that is a bonus.

The veterinarians and staff at Pawsitive are the absolute best and took fantastic care of my little girls. Toward the end of one of their lives when my girl had a number of different chronic illnesses and vitamin deficiencies, Dr. Perry kept finding therapies that helped to stabilize her and give her a few more weeks of quality time at home. The staff there are really helpful, vet visits are quick with very little waiting (which is great for pets who get stressed at the vet), and they really care about the people and animals that they serve. I can't recommend them enough

Dr. Coletti is by far the smartest & kindest veterinarian I have ever met (in 30 years of bringing my pets to various vets all over NYC).

Dr. Coletti is the BEST vet in NYC!!!

We ONLY schedule appointments for Dr. Coletti to treat our pets now because she’s truly exceptional and trust her judgement.

Linda, our 2 year old Cavalier adores her too! 🐶😺😺

Front desk staff are friendly & quick to check us in & out.
Very unprofessional staff. So many mistakes with the paperwork and billing. Doctor "couldn't" be reached. Excuse after excuse regarding the records.
Heard about this place on channel 12 news five star plays cutest dog was whiskey sour I saw on Sunday today i want to adopt her
If they try to book you with dr Colleti, reschedule.
Extremely friendly staff and good prices

Been going to PAWSitive since 2014 ever since I got my super cool best friend.

My super cool best friend also has a super cool aunt that ended up working there a few years later as a vet tech.

Everyone there is super helpful, nice, gracious and deals with a lot of caca poopoo.

I highly recommend. They also recommend calling or emailing to set up schedules.

Overall the place is decent so I want to say this review is for the handling of my pet by Dr. Sallama. I would like to say the ladies at the front desk are extremely polite and helpful, so my commentary is not about them. Nor is my commentary about the other vets there. A couple of months ago, I took my pet in for his annual physical. I noticed a mass near one his legs so I mentioned it in the required paperwork and asked if it could be examined. I went home and hours later, I get a call back. Sallama told me that she didn't do blood work, or vaccinations, nothing at all. She didn't even check the mass. Zilch. She proceeded to give me a litany of solutions but never pinpointing or suggesting one. All she did was prescribe a painkiller and told me to come back in a couple of weeks. In the interim, I sought a second opinion. I went over to Pet Haven and by this time the mass had swelled. The vet there diagnosed the issue as a tumor (and, sadly, an abscess ruptured while my cat was on the operating table). Unfortunately, I had to put my pet down. Had she settled on one solution such as an X-ray, who knows how this could have turned out. She is completely unprofessional. I spent over $100 for nothing. Please don't use this vet (Sallama).

I was on hold for an hour.
They took me off hold. Then proceeded to laugh in disbelief I was still on hold.
Yes, I was on hold for my sick cat because I thought this place would provide the best service.
Cleary I was wrong.

The best vet I've been to they showed 100% care and interest when I brought in my deceased cat to be cremated and buried definitely recommend pawsitive veterinarian plus the cat in there is really friendly
Not a good vet at all. Very money hungry and will misdiagnose and/or mishandle your pet. You’ve been forewarned.
Been coming here for 5+ years!! Staff is welcoming and caring. Vets are knowledgeable and quick. Recommend!

This is an AMAZING place! Take your pets here. Dr Coletti is extraordinarily intelligent and caring.  Kelly is exceptional at her job and pays attention to detail.  Dawn and Eileen bent over backwards to accomodate me and my sweet cat - they went above and beyond to help me out where most vet places would have turned us away immediately.  I am so thankful that I found this place and glad that I have a new place to take my cats.

PAWSitive is the best! We switched to this small, local veterinary practice because it came highly recommended and it is a 10 minute walk from our house. We are so glad that we did! Everyone on staff is very welcoming, friendly and caring. Dr. Perry takes plenty of time to explain things, both in the office and in follow up calls.  Communication with the support staff has been great-- they are quite responsive to our emails and calls. Our dog barks a lot at the vet and can be quite annoying, but everyone cheerfully tolerates it. We feel that their fees are quite fair compared to the larger, more high tech practice we formerly used.

Pawsitive is phenomenal! We bring our 3 animals here and they are so loving and caring of all our fur babies and work really well with our anxious pup and actually accept him as his difficult self and don't make us or him feel bad. Also …
